why: Plates within distance d are connected, and collecting one plate takes its whole connected component, so the answer is the number of connected components. With n <= 1000, check all pairs (compare squared distances) and union them.
hints: One second clears one whole component, so count components.
Two plates are adjacent when dx^2 + dy^2 <= d^2. Compare squares to avoid sqrt and float error.
Run DSU over n plates and test all n(n-1)/2 pairs, decrementing the component count on each successful union. O(n^2 * alpha).
pitfalls: d = 0 joins only plates at identical coordinates.
Using math.sqrt and float comparison can misjudge exact boundary cases.
